To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Word2Vec algorithm is better than GloVe for word analogy tasks, (2) the Word2vec algorithm is more robust against the morphological richness of the language, (3) the GloVe algorithm is better in capturing morphological relations between words and (4) the performance of both algorithms can be further improved with the addition of the morphological information to the input corpus
1) The Word2Vec algorithm performs better than GloVe on our Czech word analogy corpus, and 2) the Word2Vec algorithm learns the morphosyntactic properties of Czech words, while GloVe does not.
• The word embeddings are able to capture morphosyntactic relations, but the performance of these models is not satisfactory in the case of morphologically rich languages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following tasks: • We create the new corpus for word analogies for Czech.
the following questions: How do word embeddings of Czech words behave on analogy task? What is the effect of morphological richness of Czech on embeddings?

the following questions: (a) how well the state-of-the-art algorithms can learn the morphosyntactic properties of words and phrases in a morphologically rich language, and (b) how well they can capture the syntactic, semantic and morphosyntactic relationships between words and phrases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the word embeddings are a useful tool for the NLP tasks in Czech.
the Czech language is very well suited for word embedding algorithms.
the word embedding algorithms can be successfully applied to Czech words and phrases, and the results are comparable with the results on English words and phrases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results are very promising.
the results of word embedding methods on our Czech corpus are comparable to results of English word embedding models.
word analogy tasks are very suitable for inspecting the quality of Czech word embeddings, but the task is not very suitable for comparing the quality of different word embedding methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the state-of-the-art methods are able to capture the syntactic and morphological properties of Czech, but not so much the semantic properties.
the Czech word embedding methods are able to capture the morphological properties of Czech language and to learn morphological and syntactical relationships between the words.
word analogy tasks can be useful in exploring the behavior of the word embeddings in languages with rich morphology.
